rules: INSPIRE Index Polygons is an open-source HM Land Registry dataset developed to comply with the INSPIRE Directive.
The dataset contains locations of freehold registered property in England and Wales.
INSPIRE Index Polygons is a subset of HM Land Registry's Index Polygons database for freehold land and property.
HM Land Registry divides INSPIRE Index Polygons into separate files for each local-authority area in England and Wales.
A polygon on a local-authority boundary can appear in both relevant local-authority files.
INSPIRE polygons show the position and indicative extent of a registered property rather than a definitive legal boundary.
Each INSPIRE Index Polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
A Land Registry-INSPIRE ID relates the polygon to a registered title.
HM Land Registry says an INSPIRE ID can be used with Find a Property to obtain title registration and plan information.
The exact extent of land in a registered title cannot be established from INSPIRE Index Polygons alone.
HM Land Registry states that the individual title plan is needed to identify the registered-title extent.
A registered title has one title number but may contain several separate polygons.
Each separate polygon within a registered title has its own Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
Absence of a Land Registry-INSPIRE ID can mean land is not registered.
Absence of a Land Registry-INSPIRE ID can also reflect leasehold or another tenure excluded from INSPIRE.
INSPIRE polygons and attributes are available for reuse under the Open Government Licence.
HM Land Registry states that OGL reuse is free.
Failure to comply with OGL conditions ends the rights granted under the licence.
Reuse requires HM Land Registry Crown copyright and database-right attribution.
Reuse of INSPIRE polygon geometry also requires the specified Ordnance Survey attribution.
HM Land Registry asks reusers to link to the INSPIRE conditions where possible.
The INSPIRE dataset is updated on the first Sunday of each month.
Each monthly INSPIRE publication shows data from the previous month.
Current INSPIRE files remain accessible until the following monthly publication replaces them.
HM Land Registry publishes INSPIRE files as GML and says GIS software is needed to view them.
HM Land Registry captures polygon geometry against the British National Grid.
HM Land Registry identifies British National Grid as EPSG:27700 in its GML projection guidance.
QGIS can reproject HM Land Registry GML from British National Grid to other coordinate reference systems.
HM Land Registry gives WGS 84 Pseudo Mercator EPSG:3857 as an example mapping target used by Google and Bing.
HM Land Registry warns that converting British National Grid to WGS84 can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
The Planning Data API provides access to more than 100 planning and housing datasets for England through one interface.
A coordinate query constructs a point from the supplied latitude and longitude.
Coordinate search returns entities whose geometry intersects the constructed point.
A coordinate query can include multiple dataset parameters.
When multiple datasets are requested the API returns matches from any selected dataset.
The q parameter can search by postcode.
The q parameter can search by Unique Property Reference Number.
Planning Data recommends UPRN search as more precise than a coordinate for registered properties.
Entity results can include the name field.
Entity results can include the dataset field.
Entity results can include the start-date field.
Entity results can include WKT geometry.
Entity results can include a WKT point.
Planning Data warns that an empty result does not prove that no planning constraints exist.
Planning Data states that data coverage varies by area.
The documentation's local-planning-authority example retrieves 337 LPAs with a limit of 500.
The geometry_entity parameter can filter results using the geometry of another Planning Data entity.
The geometry_relation value within is documented for finding entities inside another entity boundary.
Planning Data says the planning-application specification is currently in development.
Local planning authorities are not currently required to share application data to that developing specification.
Planning-application searches support start_date_year.
Planning-application searches support start_date_month.
Planning-application searches support start_date_day.
Planning Data documents start_date_match=since for recent-application filtering.
Raw spatial searches accept WKT geometry.
Planning Data says WKT query coordinates should use WGS84 EPSG:4326.
The geometry_relation parameter supports within, equals, disjoint, intersects, touches, contains, covers, coveredby, overlaps and crosses.
Large result sets use offset pagination and the documentation recommends incrementing offset by the limit value.
Planning Data responses can include pre-built next, previous, first and last pagination links.

Portfolio screening has no batch endpoint; Planning Data recommends one request per property with polite rate limiting, while large portfolios should use bulk downloads and local spatial intersections.
The Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1m is a raster elevation model.
The DTM 1m covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The DTM 1m has 1 metre spatial resolution.
The DTM 1m is produced from the last or only laser pulse returned to the sensor.
DTM production removes surface objects from the DSM to model the terrain surface.
Environment Agency DTM production uses bespoke algorithms for surface-object removal.
Environment Agency DTM production also uses manual editing.
The current DTM 1m composite described by the record was produced in 2022.
The DTM 1m combines Time Stamped archive surveys with National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist, the newest and best-resolution source is selected for the composite.
Where source data is resampled before merging, the DTM composite uses bilinear interpolation.
The 2022 DTM 1m composite contains surveys from 6 June 2000 through 2 April 2022.
Environment Agency metadata index catalogues identify which source survey supplied a location in the composite.
The DTM 1m is downloadable as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
DTM elevations are represented in metres relative to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using the OSTN15 transformation chain.
The Environment Agency states LIDAR vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
The DTM 1m is available under the Open Government Licence.
The DTM 1m record identifies annual update frequency.
The DTM 1m coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The DTM 1m metadata identifier is 13787b9a-26a4-4775-8523-806d13af58fc.
The DTM 1m record exposes WMS, WCS, WMTS and an OGC API Features service.
Defra's Data Services Platform uses WCS as an OGC open standard for retrieving multidimensional coverage data.
Defra states its LIDAR WCS services use WCS version 2.0.1.
Defra states that WCS provides raw pixel values such as elevation while WMS provides a summarised elevation view.
Defra changed composite LIDAR service endpoints to remove the release-year suffix so future updates can use persistent URLs.
The documented persistent DTM 1m WCS endpoint is /spatialdata/lidar-composite-digital-terrain-model-dtm-1m/wcs.
Defra documents a WCS NoData value of -3.4028235e+38 in returned GeoTIFFs.
The Environment Agency DSM 1m includes heights of vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as terrain.
The Environment Agency DTM 2m carries the same published plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE LIDAR vertical-accuracy statement and uses EPSG:27700.
The retired 25cm composite DTM record states that the 25cm composite was replaced by a 1m product while time-stamped archive data remains available.
The source DTM for OS Terrain products is captured as a triangulated irregular network.
The source TIN is created using mass points, breaklines and/or automated techniques in a photogrammetric environment.
Ordnance Survey describes the TIN as capable of retaining feature edges more accurately than a grid.
OS Terrain 50 grid and contour forms are both interpolated from the source TIN model.
OS Terrain 50 minimum coverage extends to the low-water mark.
For England and Wales, the OS Terrain 50 low-water reference is Mean Low Water.
OS Terrain 50 source terrain is divided into urban/major communication routes, rural, and mountain/moorland accuracy classes.
The bare-earth source surface uses Eastings and Northings in OSGB36 and z values in metres.
Most OS Terrain 50 source heights are relative to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
The bare-earth model excludes buildings.
The bare-earth model excludes supported structures such as bridges and viaducts where an air gap exists.
The bare-earth model excludes vegetation.
Ground-level obstructions such as sufficiently significant dams, breakwaters, groynes, revetments and earthworks can be treated as part of the bare-earth surface.
Only permanent terrain features expected to remain until the next revision period or longer are modelled.
Underground features are not recorded in the DTM and overhead features are removed.
OS Terrain 50 is intended to be free of spikes and wells that do not reflect real-world terrain.
Most OS Terrain 50 data should present without visible tile edges, although small edges can occur and tidal areas can contain local tidal differences.
Major road carriageways and railway track beds are modelled to reflect their real-world shape and smoothness.
Contained flat-water bodies greater than 0.7 hectares are modelled with a flat surface at the lowest surrounding height.
OS Terrain 50 grid heights are calculated at pixel centres.
OS Terrain 50 grid tiles do not overlap and do not share common edge values.
OS Terrain 50 ASCII grid rows run west to east with 200 pixels per row.
Each OS Terrain 50 grid pixel is 50 metres by 50 metres.
OS Terrain 50 grid height values are supplied to the nearest 0.1 metre.
Per-tile OS Terrain 50 XML metadata follows the GEMINI metadata standard.
OS Terrain 50 per-tile metadata identifies British National Grid EPSG:27700 and Ordnance Datum Newlyn EPSG:5701.
The OS Downloads API lets clients discover and download OS OpenData products and product metadata.
OS Downloads API OpenData endpoints do not require an API key.
The OS Downloads API download endpoint accepts area filters including National Grid square TQ.
When redirect is requested and exactly one OpenData download matches, the OS Downloads API documents an HTTP 307 redirect to the actual download.
